section: Reservation - constitutional basis, Indra Sawhney, creamy layer, EWS reservation, promotion in reservation
subsections: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus

accepted.s: The Supreme Court judgment in which case struck down the Madras Communal Government Order and led to the First Constitutional Amendment?
o: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore
Champakam Dorairajan v. State of Madras
Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India
accepted.x: In Champakam Dorairajan (1951), the Madras Communal Government Order was struck down, leading to the First Constitutional Amendment.
accepted.tq: Identify the case from the specific constitutional consequence.
accepted.sec: Reservation cases → issue decided  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore, consider the following statements:
1. Caste cannot be the sole test for determining backwardness.
2. Reservation should generally remain below 50 per cent.
3. The case upheld reservation without prescribing any requirement of reasonableness.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The judgment emphasised that reservation must be reasonable and that caste cannot be the sole test; statement 3 is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Find the false statement by testing the omitted qualification of reasonableness.
accepted.sec: Reservation cases → issue decided  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Indra Sawhney v. Union of India, the constitutional validity of the 27 per cent reservation for OBCs was upheld by a nine-judge Bench by what majority?
accepted.x: The nine-judge Bench decided Indra Sawhney by a 6:3 majority and upheld the 27 per cent OBC quota subject to exclusion of the creamy layer.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive bench-strength and majority figures together.
accepted.sec: Reservation cases → issue decided  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a holding of the Supreme Court in Indra Sawhney (1992)?
o: A general ceiling of 50 per cent on reservations
Reservation in promotions for backward classes as a general rule
Exclusion of the creamy layer from OBC reservation
Establishment of a permanent body for backward classes
accepted.x: Indra Sawhney did not permit reservation in promotions as a general rule. It upheld 27 per cent OBC reservation, excluded the creamy layer, prescribed a 50 per cent ceiling subject to exceptional cases, and directed creation of a permanent backward-classes body.
accepted.tq: Eliminate the option that reverses the case’s principal limitation.
accepted.sec: Reservation cases → issue decided  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
The judgment in M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006) upheld the constitutional amendments relating to reservation in promotion subject to which conditions?
1. Backwardness must be established.
2. Inadequate representation must be supported by quantifiable data.
3. Administrative efficiency must be considered.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three conditions were recognised in M. Nagaraj: backwardness, inadequate representation supported by quantifiable data, and preservation of administrative efficiency.
accepted.tq: Treat a complete list of conditions as correct only when every condition belongs to the judgment.
accepted.sec: Reservation cases → issue decided  [APPSC]

accepted.s: M. Nagaraj v. Union of India is associated with upholding which of the following amendments, subject to conditions?
accepted.x: M. Nagaraj (2006) upheld the 77th and 85th Constitutional Amendments concerning reservation in promotion, subject to specified constitutional conditions.
accepted.tq: Match the case with the precise amendment pair.
accepted.sec: Reservation cases → issue decided  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India (2008):
1. It upheld the 93rd Constitutional Amendment.
2. It upheld the 2006 law concerning reservation in State and aided institutions.
3. It held that the creamy layer among OBCs need not be excluded.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The creamy layer had to be excluded, so statement 3 is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Spot the reversed position on creamy-layer exclusion.
accepted.sec: Reservation cases → issue decided  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (November 2022), consider the following statements:
1. The EWS reservation was upheld by a 3:2 majority.
2. The 50 per cent ceiling was held to apply to backward-class reservations, but not to EWS reservation.
3. The judgment was delivered unanimously.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The EWS reservation was upheld in Janhit Abhiyan by a 3:2 majority. The 50 per cent ceiling was treated as applicable to backward-class reservations and not to EWS; statement 3 is false because the Bench was divided.
accepted.tq: Use the majority figure to reject the absolute word in the third statement.
accepted.sec: Reservation cases → issue decided  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court’s decision in Jaishri Laxmanrao Patil v. State of Maharashtra (2021) primarily concerned which issue?
o: Validity of the Maratha reservation exceeding the 50 per cent ceiling
Validity of reservation for SC converts to Christianity
Exclusion of the creamy layer from EWS reservation
accepted.x: The Maratha quota was struck down for crossing the 50 per cent ceiling without exceptional circumstances.
accepted.tq: Identify the case from its distinctive reservation group and ceiling issue.
accepted.sec: Reservation cases → issue decided  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the effect of the 105th Constitutional Amendment (2021) in relation to the Maratha reservation judgment?
o: It removed the 50 per cent ceiling in all reservation matters.
It abolished the Central list of SEBCs.
It reversed the reading of the 102nd Amendment that had restricted the States’ power to identify SEBCs.
It prohibited States from maintaining backward-class lists.
accepted.x: The 105th Amendment reversed the interpretation of the 102nd Amendment in the Maratha case and restored the States’ power to identify socially and educationally backward classes.
accepted.tq: Test the constitutional amendment as a corrective response to a judicial interpretation.
accepted.sec: Reservation cases → issue decided  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Case)
A. Champakam Dorairajan
B. M.R. Balaji
C. M. Nagaraj
D. Jarnail Singh

List-II (Principal issue)
1. Conditions for reservation in promotion
2. Madras Communal Government Order
3. Caste not being the sole test and reservation below 50 per cent
4. Creamy layer in SC/ST promotions

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Champakam Dorairajan concerned the Communal Government Order; M.R. Balaji concerned caste and the 50 per cent principle; M. Nagaraj concerned promotional reservation conditions; Jarnail Singh concerned creamy layer in SC/ST promotions.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure case-issue pairs and eliminate incompatible codes.
accepted.sec: Reservation cases → issue decided  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, which group is associated with aboriginal tribes, Vimukta Jatis and nomadic groups?
accepted.x: BC-A comprises aboriginal tribes, Vimukta Jatis and nomadic groups and has a 7 per cent quota.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related BC group labels and their social composition.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to the Andhra Pradesh BC groups?
o: BC-E — aboriginal tribes and nomadic groups
accepted.x: BC-D consists of other classes. BC-B comprises vocational or occupational groups, BC-C comprises SC converts to Christianity, and BC-E comprises socially and educationally backward Muslims.
accepted.tq: Use the group-composition pairs to detect swapped categories.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to BC reservation in Andhra Pradesh:
1. BC-A — 7 per cent
2. BC-B — 10 per cent
3. BC-C — 1 per cent
4. BC-D — 7 per cent
5. BC-E — 4 per cent
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All five pairs are correct. The respective shares are BC-A 7 per cent, BC-B 10 per cent, BC-C 1 per cent, BC-D 7 per cent and BC-E 4 per cent.
accepted.tq: Check every numerical pair individually before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The BC-E category in Andhra Pradesh was added through which measure and in which year?
accepted.x: BC-E was added by the Andhra Pradesh Act of 2007. Earlier lists commonly included only BC-A to BC-D.
accepted.tq: Match the category’s introduction with the specific legal instrument and year.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to the Andhra Pradesh Muslim quota in chronological order:
A. The 2004 quota was struck down.
B. The 2005 quota was struck down.
C. The 2007 Act providing a 4 per cent quota was enacted.
D. The 2007 Act was struck down by the Andhra Pradesh High Court in 2010.
accepted.x: The 2004 and 2005 quotas were struck down first, followed by the 2007 Act providing 4 per cent reservation, which was struck down by the High Court in 2010.
accepted.tq: Fix the years first and then arrange the two earlier quota decisions.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What was the effect of the Supreme Court’s interim order concerning the 4 per cent reservation for backward Muslim groups in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It permanently approved the quota without further judicial examination.
It allowed the quota to continue pending consideration by a Constitution Bench.
It converted the quota into an EWS reservation.
It abolished the quota immediately after the High Court judgment.
accepted.x: Although the Andhra Pradesh High Court struck down the 2007 Act in 2010, the Supreme Court permitted the 4 per cent quota to continue by an interim order pending a Constitution Bench.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an interim continuation from final constitutional approval.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Kapu reservation proposal is correct?
1. The Justice Manjunatha Commission was constituted in 2016.
2. A 2017 Bill proposed 5 per cent reservation for Kapus as BC-F.
3. The proposal was approved by the Centre.
4. In 2019, Kapus received 5 per cent reservation within the 10 per cent EWS quota, which was later withdrawn by the succeeding government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The Centre never approved the 2017 BC-F proposal, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong authority-action statement among otherwise connected facts.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The combined quota shares of BC-A, BC-B, BC-C, BC-D and BC-E in Andhra Pradesh amount to:
accepted.x: The shares are 7 per cent, 10 per cent, 1 per cent, 7 per cent and 4 per cent respectively, totalling 29 per cent.
accepted.tq: Add the category-wise figures rather than confusing them with the local-body quota.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s: After 1956, which arrangement was made in relation to backward-class lists in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Separate lists were prepared only for Rayalaseema and Coastal Andhra.
Separate BC lists were maintained for Andhra and Telangana, containing 86 castes for Andhra.
A single list was prepared for the entire State without regional distinction.
BC lists were abolished and replaced by the EWS list.
accepted.x: After 1956, separate backward-class lists existed for Andhra and Telangana; the Andhra list contained 86 castes.
accepted.tq: Test the regional administrative distinction and the associated number together.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What was provided by the 1963 Government Order relating to backward classes in Andhra Pradesh?
o: 5 per cent reservation for Kapus as BC-F
4 per cent reservation for backward Muslims
20 per cent of local-body seats for BCs
25 per cent of medical seats for 139 castes
accepted.x: The 1963 Government Order provided 25 per cent of medical seats for 139 castes.
accepted.tq: Match the Government Order with its sector, percentage and caste count.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Sukhdev case concerning backward-class reservation in Andhra Pradesh resulted in which of the following conclusions?
o: Caste alone could not be the basis, and 112 classes were identified using poverty, residence and occupation.
All reservation for backward classes was unconstitutional.
Caste alone could be the basis for identifying backward classes.
Reservation could be based only on residence.
accepted.x: The High Court held in the Sukhdev case that caste alone could not be the basis; consequently, 112 classes were listed using poverty, residence and occupation as considerations.
accepted.tq: Link the judicial principle with the resulting classification exercise.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission and framed the A-D grouping along with a 25 per cent quota?
accepted.x: The Anantharaman Commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission; its report was submitted in 1970 and it framed the A-D grouping and a 25 per cent quota.
accepted.tq: Identify the commission from its distinctive first-commission and grouping role.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Muralidhara Rao Commission?
o: It was constituted in 2016 to examine Kapu reservation only.
It decided the constitutional validity of EWS reservation in 2022.
It took charge on 27 January 1982, reviewed BC reservation and examined inclusion of minorities.
accepted.x: The Muralidhara Rao Commission took charge on 27 January 1982, reviewed BC reservation, examined minority inclusion and contributed to a higher total quota.
accepted.tq: Use the commission’s date and subject of inquiry to distinguish it from other bodies.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation for BCs in Andhra Pradesh local bodies:
1. NTR introduced a 20 per cent BC quota in 1984.
2. The quota was raised to 34 per cent for polls held in 1995, 2001, 2006 and 2013.
3. It was subsequently reduced to 24.15 per cent under Government Orders 176, 559 and 560.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the quota began at 20 per cent in 1984, rose to 34 per cent for the specified elections, and was later reduced to 24.15 per cent under the cited Government Orders.
accepted.tq: Track the changing percentage chronologically and retain the order-specific details.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the stated current arrangement for Andhra Pradesh local bodies, the BC quota is:
o: 34 per cent in rural and 33.33 per cent in urban local bodies
29 per cent in rural and 34 per cent in urban local bodies
33.33 per cent in rural and 34 per cent in urban local bodies
24.15 per cent in rural and 20 per cent in urban local bodies
accepted.x: The stated arrangement provides 34 per cent reservation in rural local bodies and 33.33 per cent in urban local bodies.
accepted.tq: Compare the rural and urban figures without reversing their order.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s: G.O. Rt. No. 1065 dated 19 August 2026 relates to BC reservation in urban local-body elections under which laws?
o: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 and the Municipalities Act, 1965
The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 and the Municipalities Act, 1965
The AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 and the Municipalities Act, 1965
The AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1965 and the Panchayat Raj Act, 1994
accepted.x: G.O. Rt. No. 1065 dated 19 August 2026 concerns urban local-body polls under the AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 and the Municipalities Act, 1965.
accepted.tq: Match the Government Order with the correct pair of statutes and date.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
The Supreme Court’s triple test for OBC reservation in local bodies requires:
1. A dedicated commission to examine backwardness.
2. Determination of the reservation proportion local-body-wise.
3. Keeping the total reservation within the 50 per cent ceiling.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three requirements form the triple test: a dedicated commission, local-body-wise proportional determination, and compliance with the overall 50 per cent ceiling.
accepted.tq: Recognise a judicial test as a cumulative set of mandatory conditions.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The earlier 34 per cent reservation for BCs in Andhra Pradesh local bodies was struck down primarily because it:
o: Was introduced through a Constitutional Amendment
Was confined to urban local bodies only
accepted.x: The earlier 34 per cent local-body reservation was struck down for breaching the overall reservation ceiling.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional limitation triggered by the percentage claimed.
accepted.sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]
